newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money jumps on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money jumps on rate hike.

text.p: Manila overnight money soared to an average of 12.03125 from 11.3125 percent on Thursday after the 75 basis-point increase in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 12 percent, traders said.
The Central Bank said its move was to protect the peso against any backlash from the problems of the Thai baht.
"This is a temporary blip in interest rates," a foreign bank dealer said.
Done rates rose to a higher band of 12.5/12.03125 percent, with 27 lenders and 16 borrowers. Volume was higher at 12.38 billion from 11.86 billion pesos.
In the secondary market, there was little activity as banks decided to stay on the sidelines after the increase in the Central Bank's key rate.
"There's no rush to buy and no one wants to sell at this point," a trader said.
Banks want to wait before positioning, dealers said.
A Reuters poll of nine financial institutions gave bids of 10.6785/10.80 percent and offers of 10.55/10.65 for the three-month bills.
